inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 252.05M common shares on the Q2 2026 10-Q cover (2026-07-10) plus 0.40M dilutive securities (IncrementalCommonSharesAttributableToShareBasedPaymentArrangements, Q2 2026). Q2 2026 diluted weighted average was 253.86M; the point-in-time count is lower because $614.5M of H1-2026 buybacks retired ~2.5M shares. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: ShareBasedCompensation $79.448M add-back plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $31.809M in financing (XBRL companyfacts). WCN publishes no combined equity-award figure in its adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation (it adds back only fair-value changes to equity awards, not the base expense), so the two lines are summed per the method.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $505.5M; H1-2026 $614.5M. WCN is an active repurchaser, so the flat share count is being funded in cash, not a modelling convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~0.70 (low-beta essential service) x ERP 4.5% = cost of equity ~7.35%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (WCN senior notes) x (1-24%) = ~3.8%; market weights E ~$38.8B / D ~$9.2B = 81/19 give a CAPM WACC of ~6.7%. Rounded UP to 7.0% as a modest charge for the premium-multiple de-rating risk the Analysis flags. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: lease cost sits in cost of operations inside EBITDA (so inside the projected flows), and the $311M operating-lease liability (FY2025 10-K) is therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases ($15M) are immaterial and already within total debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: MinorityInterest is $0 at FY2025 and Q2 2026 (XBRL); no NCI adjustment.
inputs.interest_income_note: WCN is a net-debt company ($9.2B net debt vs $1.1B owner FCF); interest income is immaterial (InterestIncomeOther carries no material tags) and is not deducted. The net-cash rule does not apply.
inputs.unlevered_note: last_fcf (1123.6) is the LEVERED owner FCF on the reported basis (OCF - capex - SBC - equity-award taxes) and is the anchor every downstream consumer reads. The engine's projections are UNLEVERED (EBIT x (1-t) + D&A - capex +/- WC) and net debt is deducted once at the end, so year-1 projected FCF (~$1.6B) sits above last_fcf by roughly the after-tax interest paid ($308M FY2025 x (1-0.24) = ~$235M) plus the FY2026 EBITDA step-up. Cross-check: FY2026 guidance adj FCF midpoint $1,425M + after-tax interest ~$258M - SBC incl. taxes ~$115M - asset-sale proceeds ~$10M = ~$1,558M unlevered owner FCF; the base-case year-1 component build lands ~2-3% above that, with the gap being the 19% cash tax rate on unlevered EBIT versus WCN's bonus-depreciation-sheltered actual (~17%).
inputs.ma_treatment: ROLL-UP TREATMENT (the method files carry no specific rule, so this is the stated position): acquisitions are EXCLUDED ON BOTH SIDES in every scenario. Growth paths after the guided FY2026 are organic only (core price + volume + RNG/E&P ramp); acquisition outlays (PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired $818M FY2025, ~$2.2B FY2024, $310M H1-2026) are NOT charged as capex. Crediting acquired revenue without the spend would overstate value; charging the spend without the revenue would understate it. The spread WCN earns buying private haulers at ~10-11x EBITDA against its own ~14-15x multiple is left as un-modelled optionality and is named in the bull narrative rather than priced. FY2026's 6.0% guided growth does include ~1.5pp of rollover from deals already closed; that is kept because the cash has already left the balance sheet at 2026-06-30.
inputs.ebitda_definition: ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC adjusted EBITDA (the engine deducts SBC separately). WCN's own adjusted EBITDA is AFTER equity-based compensation expense and adds back ~$48M/yr of closure/post-closure accretion. Translation: company FY2026 guide 33.2-33.3% + SBC expense ~0.8% - accretion ~0.5% (a real deferred cash cost, charged here) = ~33.5-33.6% engine basis; base year 1 uses 33.4% for a small margin of safety.
inputs.guidance_fy2026: Q2 2026 release (raised): revenue $10.02-10.05B; adjusted EBITDA $3.33-3.34B (33.2-33.3%); net cash from operations $2.63-2.68B; adjusted FCF $1.40-1.45B; total solid-waste pricing ~6-7% against volumes ~-1.9%; >$100M annualised acquired revenue closed with ~$30M more of franchise deals expected Q3.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (year-5 margin still ramping in base and bull). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 1-2 (operating company; US filer so the non-US adaptations file was not needed: USD/USD, ASC 842 leases already in EBITDA, zero NCI, no excluded income, SBC-positive). Fresh build, no prior DCF or memory entry. Volatile-price check: the quote is a Friday regular close, not an after-hours print. Balance sheet and share count are from the latest filing (Q2 2026 10-Q). Horizon FY2026-FY2035.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case organic path (FY2027-FY2035 average of core price + volume); NOT the equity CAGR, which is depressed by $1.5B of buybacks FY2021-25 and the FY2024 Chiquita Canyon impairment, and NOT the revenue CAGR, roughly half of which was debt-funded M&A that the model excludes on both sides
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 3.7% vs revenue 5y CAGR 11.7% and EPS 5y 39.9%: divergence >30%. Causes: (1) WCN returns capital via buybacks and dividends so book equity does not compound with the business; (2) revenue growth was roughly half M&A funded by debt (net debt $4.7B FY2020 -> $9.2B Q2 2026), which grows revenue without growing equity; (3) EPS 5y base FY2020 ($0.78) carries a $417M impairment and FY2024 ($2.39) carries the Chiquita Canyon landfill charges, so the EPS CAGR is noise. The 3y figures (revenue 9.5%, EPS 8.8%, equity 5.0%) are the cleaner read.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes): FY2020 674.8, FY2021 877.1, FY2022 1028.0, FY2023 1091.4, FY2024 1062.1, FY2025 1123.6. Owner-FCF 3y CAGR 3.0% vs reported 3.6%: SBC + equity-award taxes grew from $81.8M to $111.3M over the period, so a growing slice of reported FCF growth was paid in stock. Both series are LEVERED (after ~$300M/yr interest paid) and sit well below the unlevered flows the engine projects; FCF growth FY2022-25 was also held back by Chiquita Canyon closure cash costs and the RNG capex build-out.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the 6.0% guided midpoint ($10,035M). Thereafter organic only: core price normalises from ~6-7% toward ~4% as CPI-linked escalators reset, volumes flat-to-slightly negative then recovering, RNG and E&P adding ~0.5pp. 5.0% -> 3.0% over nine years, terminal 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC engine basis (see inputs.ebitda_definition). 33.4% in FY2026 vs the ~33.5-33.6% translation of guidance; +30bp/yr fading to +10bp/yr as price-over-cost spread persists and RNG plants reach run-rate; mature at 35.0% (= ~34% on WCN's own definition, ~150bp above FY2026 guidance).
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 capex implied by guidance (OCF midpoint 2,655 - adj FCF midpoint 1,425 + asset-sale proceeds ~10) = ~$1,240M = 12.4% of revenue; glides to 11.5% as the ~$200M+ RNG build-out completes and growth slows. D&A 13.0% (FY2025 actual, H1-2026 13.0%) drifts to 12.5% as acquired-intangible amortisation ($202M FY2025) runs off with no new M&A modelled.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 cash taxes $221M on $1,418M pretax = 15.6%; on an unlevered basis (adding back the ~$80M interest shield) ~17%. GAAP ETR 24.1%. Bonus depreciation (made permanent in 2025) keeps cash below book while capex grows, so the ramp runs 19% -> 23% by year 5 rather than straight to statutory.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables (~14% of revenue) grow faster than deferred revenue (+$34M FY2025) and payables; growth consumes a little cash. -5% of the revenue change.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 7.0% / 2.5% = 22.8x; the 20x house cap binds. Recorded as cap-bound.

bull.growth_rationale: Top of FY2026 guide plus Q3 franchise closings; pricing holds 5-6% on the exclusive/franchise half of the book, C&D and special-waste volumes turn positive, E&P Permian/Bakken expansion and a dozen RNG plants add ~1pp. Still organic only; the M&A spread is NOT in these numbers.
bull.margin_rationale: Price-led growth plus AI routing/pricing tools and RNG credits lift the engine-basis margin to 36.5% (~35.5% on WCN's definition) by year 9.
bull.capex_rationale: RNG build complete by FY2028; capex intensity falls to 11.0%, D&A follows down to 12.2% as amortisation runs off.
bull.tax_rationale: Bonus depreciation shelter persists longer with sustained fleet/landfill investment; cash rate tops out at 22%.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the bottom of guidance; then CPI escalators reset to ~3% pricing, C&D/special-waste/E&P volumes keep falling 1-2% as construction and drilling soften, recycling commodity prices stay weak: organic growth ~2-3%.
bear.margin_rationale: PFAS/CERCLA leachate treatment and remediation costs (the Analysis' one HIGH-severity risk) plus recurring Chiquita-type landfill 'other operating items' compress the engine-basis margin 140bp to 32.0%; SBC does not decline as a share of revenue.
bear.capex_rationale: PFAS treatment capex and landfill-cell construction keep capex at 12.5-12.8% with no RNG taper; D&A flat at 13.0%.
bear.tax_rationale: Cash rate converges on the 24% GAAP ETR by year 5 as bonus-depreciation shelter fades with slower capex growth.
bear.terminal_rationale: Cap lowered to 18x for a 2%-grower; Gordon at 7.0%/2.0% = 20.4x so the cap binds.

scenario_narratives.base: WCN keeps doing what it has done: price ahead of cost in secondary and franchise markets where it holds #1/#2 share, hold volumes roughly flat, and widen margins ~30bp a year while the RNG plants reach run-rate. FY2026 lands on the raised guide (revenue ~$10.0B, adjusted EBITDA ~33.25%, adjusted FCF ~$1.4B). Growth decelerates from 6% to 3% as CPI-linked escalators reset; margin (engine basis) matures at 35%; capex intensity eases from 12.4% to 11.5% once the RNG build-out is done; cash tax ramps from 19% to 23%. Acquisitions are excluded on both sides. The terminal value is cap-bound at 20x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The two things WCN specifically needs go right: pricing stays sticky at 5-6% because half the collection book is under exclusive/franchise contracts with CPI-plus escalators, and C&D/special-waste/E&P volumes recover with construction and drilling activity. RNG credits and AI-driven routing/pricing lift the engine-basis margin to 36.5%; capex falls to 11% of revenue after FY2028. Still organic only: the real bull axis the model does NOT price is the roll-up spread (buying private haulers at ~10-11x EBITDA against WCN's ~14-15x, $0.8-2.2B a year), which is value creation that shows up only if the deals keep coming at those multiples.
scenario_narratives.bear: PFAS/CERCLA becomes a real cost of owning 93 landfills: leachate treatment, remediation and litigation push 'impairments and other operating items' from a Chiquita one-off into a recurring line, and PFAS capex keeps intensity at 12.5-12.8% with no RNG taper. Pricing normalises to ~3% as inflation fades while C&D, special-waste and E&P volumes keep falling 1-2%, so organic growth drops to 2-3%. Margin compresses 140bp to 32%; cash tax converges on the 24% book rate. No solvency question (net debt/EBITDA ~2.75-3.0x, cover ~5x), so the bear is a de-rating of a premium multiple, not a going-concern case; the terminal cap is lowered to 18x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 moved to 20/50/30. Bear up 5pp because PFAS/CERCLA is the Analysis' one high-severity risk and is industry-wide, slow-moving and uncapped, and because current 6-7% pricing is above what CPI-linked escalators will deliver once inflation fades. Bull down 5pp because the bull case as modelled is organic-only and already assumes two independent things (sticky pricing AND a volume recovery); the roll-up spread that would justify a higher bull weight is deliberately left out of the numbers. Base 50%: WCN has met or raised guidance in most years and the business is essential-service, low-beta and contractually priced.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value WCN as a stream of unlevered owner FCF from the existing franchise, SBC and equity-award taxes fully expensed, share count held flat (funded by ~$0.5-0.6B/yr of buybacks), net debt of $9.2B deducted once, and acquisitions excluded on both sides so the price paid for growth and the growth bought cancel. A 10-year explicit horizon because margins are still ramping at year 5; a 20x owner-FCF terminal cap because WCN is a mature compounder, lowered to 18x in the bear. The current price sits well above the house value: the market is capitalising the roll-up spread and treating the premium multiple as permanent, which this model deliberately does not do. The 15% hurdle entry price is the number to act on.
key_risks_to_valuation: M&A excluded on both sides: if WCN keeps buying at ~10-11x EBITDA and the market keeps paying ~14-15x, the model under-states value by the PV of that spread; if deal multiples rise or integration slips, the exclusion flatters it.
PFAS/CERCLA remediation and leachate costs are industry-wide, slow-moving and unquantified; the bear case charges 140bp of margin and higher capex, which may be too little.
Pricing normalisation: 6-7% total pricing is inflation-era; the base assumes it fades to ~4%. Faster fade with no volume recovery is the bear path.
Cash-tax ramp from 19% to 23%: permanent bonus depreciation could keep the cash rate nearer 17% for longer (upside); a change in US tax law could lift it (downside).
WACC 7.0% rounds a 6.7% CAPM build up; each 1pp of WACC moves the base value materially given a cap-bound terminal that is ~65% of EV (see sensitivity grid).
Terminal cap at 20x owner FCF binds in every scenario; the market currently pays ~29x unlevered owner FCF, so the model embeds a de-rating by construction.
